title: wt new --dry-run --json
description: What `wt new` would create, from local state alone; it writes nothing. Printed by `wt new <type>/<work> [--base <ref>] --dry-run --json` as the only thing on stdout. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

token.description: Names the inputs of this plan; pass it to `wt new --json --expect`. Null when the plan has a problem.

configured.description: The repository has a wt configuration that parses.

types.description: The worktree types this repository declares.

defaultType.description: The type a bare work name takes.

type.description: The type the worktree would have; null when the name did not parse.

work.description: The work name; null when it did not parse or could not be derived.

branch.description: The branch the worktree would be on.

path.description: The absolute path the worktree would be created at.

base.description: What the branch would be cut from, as given with --base, else trunk.

baseCommit.description: The commit base resolves to now; null when it does not resolve.

buildCommand.description: The build command that would run; null when build initialisation is off, --no-build or --no-setup.

superset.description: wt would try to register the worktree as a Superset workspace: you opted in and SUPERSET_REGISTER is auto or on. Whether Superset is running and knows this repository is not checked.

problems.description: Why the worktree would not be created; empty when it would.

code.description: branchExists, pathExists, unknownType, invalidName, noConfiguration, configurationInvalid, branchMissing, branchCheckedOut (git gives a branch one worktree), baseMissing.
